name: Abū ʿAlī al-Ḥasan ibn Hāniʾ al-Ḥakamī, known as Abū Nuwās
summary: The great poet of ʿAbbāsid Baghdad, born in al-Ahwāz and raised in Basra, who learned the rare words from Abū Zayd and the battle-days of the Arabs from Abū ʿUbayda; his verse was cited and explained by the grammarians.
bio: Abū Nuwās was born in al-Ahwāz and grew up in Basra, a client, it is said, of al-Jarrāḥ ibn ʿAbd Allāh al-Ḥakamī. He attended Abū Zayd al-Anṣārī and wrote down the rare words from him, and learned the battle-days of the Arabs from Abū ʿUbayda; Ibn al-Anbārī includes him for that learning in the language.
He became the poet of the court of Hārūn al-Rashīd and al-Amīn in Baghdad, where he died in 196/811. Al-Sukkarī later edited his poetry with a commentary on its rare words.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 96–103
